headline: Apple Vision Pro performs first-of-its-kind hip surgery using Stryker's FDA-authorized software
summary: Stryker's SportSuite Vision app, which received FDA De Novo authorization in July, powered the procedure at Duke Health, providing surgeons with critical real-time data.
details: Medical technology company Stryker announced its SportSuite Vision app for the Apple Vision Pro was used in a milestone hip arthroscopy at Duke Health. This marks the first time the software has been put into real-world practice, following its FDA De Novo authorization on July 17.

The mixed-reality experience offered by the Vision Pro allows medical professionals to interact with a real patient and the physical environment while simultaneously accessing digital content and tools. This integration aims to create a more streamlined and informed surgical process.

During the inaugural SportSuite Vision operation, the surgeon gained access to Stryker's orthopedic surgery planning tools, arthroscopic images, and CT imaging. This critical information was available directly within the sterile field, enhancing situational awareness.

Dr. Chad Mather III, the orthopedic surgeon at Duke Health, stated that spatial computing enabled him to customize the placement of key clinical information to fit his workflow. This helped create a more comfortable and efficient operating room setup.

While the high cost and development challenges of the Vision Pro may limit mainstream adoption, this application highlights its potential in specialized medical scenarios. Such creative uses could help the headset reach its full potential in professional fields.

headline_marked: [[Accel reportedly in talks to lead $1B round for Thinking Machines]] at $40B valuation
headline: Accel reportedly in talks to lead $1B round for Thinking Machines at $40B valuation
summary: The potential funding round would value the AI lab, founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, at $40 billion, a figure below its previously sought $50 billion valuation.
details: Thinking Machines, the AI lab founded early last year by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, is reportedly in discussions to raise $1 billion. This potential fundraise would value the company at a minimum of $40 billion, according to The Information.
Existing investor Accel is reportedly in talks to lead this new funding round. This information comes from both TechCrunch's source and The Information's reporting.

If completed, this round would value Thinking Machines below the $50 billion valuation it reportedly aimed for late last year. The company's annual revenue run rate currently stands at over $100 million.

This revenue figure implies an extraordinarily high revenue multiple for the $40 billion valuation. Neither Accel nor Thinking Machines immediately responded to requests for comment regarding these reports.
In July, Thinking Machines introduced Inkling, an open-weight model. This model generates revenue by charging usage-based compute fees for adapting models on proprietary data via its Tinker platform.

The startup's previous funding round was a $2 billion seed financing, valuing the company at $12 billion. This round, led by Andreessen Horowitz and joined by Nvidia, GV, Lightspeed, and Conviction Partners, was largely backed due to the pedigree of Murati and her co-founding team of former OpenAI researchers.
